messages.subject: Stacked Bar Plot help
parts:
Hi,

I have some patient data recording their diabetes risk which is an
integer from 0 to 100.
I have used R to factor this data to provide their score as low,
intermediate1, intermediate2,high,extreme or diabetes ( =100)
The researcher would like to show the counts as a stacked bar graph,
where "Low" is on its own, Intermediate 1 and 2 are stacked, High and
Extreme are stacked and Diabetes is on its own - please see the pdf
file at http://tinyurl.com/yybygop to show the plot produced from the
code below, and a rough picture of what the researcher would like
produced. She would also like it faceted by "Unit", which I think I
know how to do, the issue is getting the plot looking like she wants
it.
I think it has to do with matching the bins above to a manual x scale
and setting the breaks where she wants them and setting position =
"stack", but I have not had any luck getting the stack happening nor
do I really understand how to get the particular colour combo as a
fill and legend.

Here is the code and data used to create the first plot. Any
assistance would be really appreciated!
Thanks.


ddata <-
read.table("http://tinyurl.com/y6wcy8j",
header=TRUE, sep=",", na.strings="NA", dec=".", strip.white=TRUE)
Hosp_D_Risk <- Hosp_D_Risk[!is.na(Hosp_D_Risk)]
Hosp_D_Risk=cut(ddata
$D_Risk,breaks=c(-1,5,5.5,10,14,14.5,19,99,99.5,100),labels=c("Low","
","Interm1","Interm2"," ","High","Extreme"," ","Diabetes"))
qplot(Hosp_D_Risk, geom="bar", fill=I("darkred")) +
opts(title="Hospital")+ xlab("Diabetes Risk Score")+ ylab("n") +
ylim(0,50)

Further to my first post.

Sorry - should have said what a fantastic package ggplot2 is!

I have travelled a little further - and added some additional
variables to the data - being the following code. This has given me
the stacked bar graph I was after, but the x axis is in alphabetical
order and the colours are not right. Any suggestions welcome??

test <- ddata
attach(test)
test$driskcat[D_Risk <=5] <- "Low"
test$driskcat[D_Risk >5 & D_Risk <=15] <- "Intermediate"
test$driskcat[D_Risk >15 & D_Risk <=99] <- "High"
test$driskcat[D_Risk >99] <- "Diabetes"
test1 <- test
attach(test1)
test1$driskscore[D_Risk <=5] <- "Low"
test1$driskscore[D_Risk > 5 & D_Risk <=10] <- "Intermediate1"
test1$driskscore[D_Risk >10 & D_Risk <=15] <- "Intermediate2"
test1$driskscore[D_Risk >15 & D_Risk <=19] <- "High"
test1$driskscore[D_Risk >19 & D_Risk <=99] <- "Extreme"
test1$driskscore[D_Risk >99] <- "Diabetes"
test2 <- subset(test1, subset=driskcat != "NA")
showData(test2, placement='-20+200', font=getRcmdr('logFont'),
maxwidth=80,
maxheight=30)
require(ggplot2)
qplot(driskcat, data=test2, geom="bar", fill=driskscore)

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Stacked Bar Plot help
parts:
The categories are being ordered alphabetically because they are
strings. If they were levels of a factor, then they maintain the
ordering in the factor levels. This is most easily done with the
cut() function (since you are dividing a continuous variable); this is
what you did in your first pass with Hosp_D_Risk. To get the colors,
you can use scale_fill_manual. Putting it all together:

ddata <- read.table("http://tinyurl.com/y6wcy8j",
header=TRUE,
sep=",",
na.strings="NA",
dec=".",
strip.white=TRUE)

ddata <- transform(ddata,
driskcat = cut(D_Risk,
c(-Inf, 5, 15, 99, Inf),
labels=c("Low","Intermediate","High","Diabetes")),
driskscore = cut(D_Risk,
c(-Inf, 5, 10, 15, 19, 99, Inf),

labels=c("Low","Intermediate1","Intermediate2","High","Extreme","Diabetes")))
require(ggplot2)
qplot(driskcat, data=ddata, geom="bar", fill=driskscore) +
scale_fill_manual("Risk Score",
values=c("green","yellow","gold","red","brown","black")) +
scale_x_discrete("Diabetes Risk Score") +
scale_y_continuous("n")

Brian, thanks so much for this - It's an elegant solution that and
teaches me and anyone else new to the environment some additional
tricks in R. Thanks again.

I eventually got there last night with the following code and trawling
through the posts. This group is a great resource.


p <-qplot(data= test2, factor(driskcat, levels=c("Low","Intermediate",
"High","Diabetes"), ordered = TRUE),
fill=factor(driskscore,
levels=c("Low","Intermediate1","Intermediate2",
"High","Extreme","Diabetes"), ordered = TRUE))

p1 <- p + geom_bar() + scale_fill_manual(name= "Risk Category",
values = c("Low" = "green","Intermediate1" = "yellow",
"Intermediate2" = "orange", "High" = "red", "Extreme" =
"darkred",
"Diabetes" = "black"))

p1 + xlab("Diabetes Risk") + ylab("n") + opts(title = "Diabetes Risk
at the Hospital")
